name: Tantuni
description: Mersin-style sautéed beef with tomato, peppers, and cumin rolled into a thin tortilla-like bread.
ingredients: a generous handful of ripe tomatoes
a handful of fresh mint, chopped
instructions: Prepare the rice pilaf base and set it aside to rest while you get the filling ready.
In a bowl, combine the beef sirloin, cucumber, sliced scallions, and dried mint, mixing well so everything is evenly seasoned.
Heat olive oil in a skillet, wok, or on a griddle over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Cook the rice pilaf until lightly golden on each side, then transfer to a warm plate.
Fry, grill, or steam the beef sirloin mixture until cooked through and lightly charred at the edges, about 15 mins.
Assemble by layering the rice pilaf with the filling, a spoonful of toasted pine nuts, and a scattering of mint.
Add a final touch of lemon wedges for extra flavor and texture.
Serve immediately while hot, with extra toasted pine nuts on the side for dipping or drizzling.
tips: Keep the olive oil hot but not smoking — a thermometer helps you nail the perfect frying or grilling temperature.
Prep all your fillings and toppings before you start cooking, since this dish comes together quickly once the heat is on.
Serve immediately for the best contrast between a crisp exterior and a warm, tender filling.
